core.title: Serve every markup-declared mutating endpoint from the declared journey space
core.given: A repo whose declared journey space (the route registry the boundary surface declares, per profile) resolves, with presentation markup anywhere (changed or not) carrying a declarative mutating-request construct whose target path is statically written
core.when: the journey space resolves; every such endpoint repo-wide is checked, not only edited files
core.then: Ensure every such endpoint is served (routed) by the surface that declares the journey space, or drop the affordance.
prefer: Add a handler in that surface matching the endpoint's method and path that checks authorization (answering with the unauthorized client error on failure) and returns the response the markup expects (e.g. the updated fragment).
If the journey does not admit the mutation, remove the affordance from markup.
avoid: Adding a mutating affordance (button/form) to markup ahead of its handler (the common cause).
Markup minting a state-advancing route the journey never admitted (a parallel, private route space); a confirmation gate, a progress indicator and a passing test do not make it routed.
Removing/renaming a route in the journey-declaring surface while existing markup still carries a static mutating endpoint for the old path.
Merely mentioning the endpoint's path text in the journey-declaring surface without a handler that serves that method and path.
unless: Read-only fetch affordances: fetching a fragment is presentation, not a journey (only the profile's mutating constructs owe a route).
Statically unresolvable targets: endpoints whose path is built by dynamic composition are skipped, not guessed (unresolvable bindings stay unjudged).
No journey space resolves: the rule does not apply (no declared route registry, so no journey space to be outside of).
core.why: Hypermedia declares its route space in markup; unbound, markup mints state-advancing routes the journey never admitted and affordances post into nothing. Mutations advance state, as journeys do, so they owe a route; reads do not.
evidence: The stack's check for this rule reports no unrouted mutating endpoint anywhere in the repo.
Every statically written mutating endpoint in the repo's markup (changed or not) is named by the surface that declares the journey space (whole path or distinctive terminal segment).
The check's result is not applicable only when no journey space resolves.
verification: Locate the journey space by the registry construct it declares (per profile), never by file name.
Collect every statically written mutating endpoint in markup repo-wide (changed or not) and flag one the journey space names nowhere.
Matching is on the whole path or its distinctive terminal segment; do not match on an arbitrary segment — that makes the rule vacuous.
Skip endpoints whose target path is built by dynamic composition: it cannot be compared to a route by text, and guessing would report on correct code (statically unresolvable bindings stay unjudged).
Do not report read-only fetch affordances: mutations only, deliberately — requiring every read to be routed by the journey space would fail ordinary hypermedia usage.
Report not-applicable when no journey space resolves — a repo with no declared journey space has no journey to be outside of.
Strict disposition, severity 4: a state-changing affordance the server never routes is not suppressible and fails the enforcing run.

values: the journey-declaring boundary surface's kinds (per roles.boundary.kinds)
a declared journey space (the boundary surface carrying the route registry) resolves in the repo
a statically written mutating endpoint in markup is named nowhere by the journey space

fires: Markup gains a mutating construct with a static target path that no handler in the journey-declaring surface routes.
A mutating affordance is added to markup ahead of its handler in the boundary surface.
A route is removed or renamed in the journey-declaring boundary surface while existing, unchanged markup still carries a static mutating endpoint for the old path.
A pre-existing static mutating endpoint in untouched markup is named nowhere by the journey space (the invariant is repo-wide, independent of what was edited).
doesNotFire: Mutating endpoints whose target path is built by dynamic composition (statically unresolvable bindings).
Repos where no journey space resolves (no declared route registry, so no journey space).
Static mutating endpoints whose whole path or distinctive terminal segment the check finds named by the journey space (check behaviour, not proof of routing).

neutralityNotes: The obligation, all three exceptions, the repo-wide (not-edited-files) scope, the matching policy (whole path or distinctive terminal segment), the skip of statically unresolvable targets, the not-applicable condition, and the strict/severity-4 disposition are stack-neutral and kept in the core. The core activation file_kind scope covers BOTH the markup kinds (idiom.markup_kinds: html, markup, jsx, tsx, template) and the journey-declaring boundary surface's kinds (roles.boundary.kinds: server_module), matching the Bun fact's list, so the server surface whose routes markup must match stays eligible. What could not be neutralized: (1) the activation 'language' fact has no neutral fact type, so it lives as profile data (tooling.languages) plus a bunOnly item; (2) the concrete construct names (hx-post/put/patch/delete, hx-get), the journey-space declaration (JOURNEY_MAP), the surface name (journey router) and the artifact kinds are profile values, never core text; (3) detector/validator ids, checker paths and the verbatim fix_hint snippet remain bunOnly with the core's verification naming the check generically; (4) no existing vocabulary key names the declaration that constitutes the journey space (idiom.routing#journey_registry proposed) or the authorization check that gates a mutating endpoint (idiom.security#authorization_check proposed — idiom.auth_guard covers authentication/principal establishment, a different decision). The Bun rule treats destructive and non-destructive mutating constructs uniformly; the core says so once and the profile supplies both key values.
